reason: Spent under another id: v3 task ts-upgrade-express-api (typescript@6.0.2/deprecate-esmoduleinterop-false) was built from exactly this TypeScript 7 hard error (TS5108 for esModuleInterop false), and its stale config and oracle are what a v4 task would use.

Re-checked against 6.0.3: the directive only names the define() emitted under module amd/umd/system (which 6.0.3 still emits with ignoreDeprecations 6.0) and is silently ignored under every module value in 6.0.3 and 7.0.2 alike, so what breaks is the removal of module amd (TS5108), the spent change typescript@7.0.2/remove-module-amd-umd-system-none (v3 ts-upgrade-slug-library).

Checked against the v4 old version: TypeScript 6.0.3 already rejects module Foo {} with the same TS1540 error as 7.0.2, ignoreDeprecations 6.0 does not suppress it, and under skipLibCheck both versions accept it in .d.ts files, so no code that compiled on 6.0.3 behaves differently on 7.0.2.

The rule only fires on `x` + newline + `/y/d` with no space between the second slash and a d/v-letter identifier: tried a regex literal meant to start a line in no-semicolon code (it parses as division, throws at runtime and no-undef already reports its operands in 10.4.1) and a deliberate multi-line division (only reported when written unspaced, e.g. `total` newline `/count/d`, which no formatter or plausible code produces; spaced divisions are not reported in either version).
